title: Heart failure: type, acuity and hypertension
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's heart failure and any related hypertension.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow up for heart failure and HTN.

HPI
Pt is a 79 y/o male presenting for routine follow up of chronic systolic heart failure and hypertension. Pt reports feeling well today. Denies shortness of breath, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Denies peripheral edema or increased weight gain. States he is adherent to current meds. Stable on home regimen.

Medication List
Lisinopril 20mg daily
Carvedilol 12.5mg BID
Furosemide 40mg daily
Spironolactone 25mg daily

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, regular rhythm. No murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs: CTAB. No crackles or wheezes.
Ext: No pedal edema.
Vitals: BP 128/78, HR 72, RR 16, SpO2 97% on RA.

Assessment
1. Chronic HFrEF: Stable. EF remains at 30%. No signs of volume overload.
2. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current meds.

Plan
Continue current medications as prescribed. Pt to monitor daily weights. F/u in 3 months for routine check.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Hypertension with heart failure is presumed linked: I11.0, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, plus the I50 code.

distractors.why: The classification presumes a causal link between hypertension and heart failure.
The type and acuity are documented: do not use I50.9.
The provider documents systolic heart failure.
